messages.author: 2d95e9975596a58a
messages.subject: SEM for a questionnaire
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am trying to fit a SEM with 1970 no-missing observations(data=ipo_1). the variables include : 
pain perception indicators(P1Q, P2Q, P3Q_r), 
pain disturbances(P4_INBD, P4_BR, P4_SL), 
emotional impairments(P5_ST,P5_HL),
side effects from pain medicine(P6_DZ, P6_SP, P6_IC, P6_NS)
pain relief(P7_r),
satisfaction(P11Q).

My first try is fit SEM as model below.
                DIS=~ P4_INBD + P4_BR + P4_SL
                EMT=~ P5_ST+P5_HS
                SIT=~ P6_NS+P6_SP+P6_IC+P6_DZ
                PAN=~ P1Q + P2Q +P3Q_r + P7Q_r
                P11Q ~ DIS + EMT + SIT +PAN

But R gave out the warning message "lavaan WARNING:
    the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!". How to fix it to get a good fit?

Thank you 
Joan


And I also run the corrplot() and scree() and get the result as below

messages.author: 08e48595b188026f
messages.subject: Re: SEM for a questionnaire
parts:
Dear Joan,

I would first try to remove P11Q and only run a CFA, to see if the problem is in the measurement model or the structural model. In any case, I think that you might think about the adequacy of your proposed factor structure. From the correlations and scree plot it seems that a 4 first order factor solution might not work. A 2 factor solution seems more in line with your data, but it depends if you can find good theoretical justification for changing the factorial structure. Note also that P1Q and P2Q do not really have a correlation with P7Q_r or P3Q_r so making them load on the same factor might not be appropriate. Maybe you can try first with exploratory factor analysis and work from there.

Regards,
Jošt
